## Svelte 5 rewrite

Closes #13273

This is super draft and it's just to play around with the output and discuss.

Please note that [the Svelte codebase is currently being rewritten for Svelte 5](https://svelte.dev/blog/runes). Changes should target Svelte 5, which lives on the default branch (`main`).

- [x] Prefix your PR title with `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, or `docs:`.
- [x] This message body should clearly illustrate what problems it solves.
- [x] Ideally, include a test that fails without this PR but passes with it.

### Tests and linting

- [x] Run the tests with `pnpm test` and lint the project with `pnpm lint`

It's not only for programmatic migration, but migration in general.

When migrating a Svelte 4 component to Svelte 5, switching to the handler as props will break all existing code that use this component with on:event directive (and this code can be out-of-control).

In 100% Svelte 5 code, `<button on:click on:blur on:focus {...$$restProps}>` could be simplified as `<button {...props}>` (and it's even better since all the handlers are spreaded).

But since I need to keep compatibility, I should add bubbles to forward events again in order to support the old `on:event` syntax from the caller : 
```svelte
<script>
    let { onclick, onblur, onfocus, ...props } = $props();
    
    const bubble = createBubbler();
</script>
<button onclick={handlers(onclick, bubble('click')}
    onblur={handlers(onblur, bubble('blur')}
    onfocus={handlers(onfocus, bubble('focus')}
    {...props}> ... </button>
```

=> A lot more verbose, even than the Svelte 4 code, and that's just an one-line component !
Additionally, this would need another rewrite in the futur when `on:event` directive will be removed.


I think that could prevent devs from migrating their codes...


In fact the Svelte 4 code is even simpler, since it can handle both `onclick` and `on:click`.

=> For "pure" Svelte 5 component, I think that `on:event` should be automatically mapped into `onevent`.

If you have this...

```svelte
<button on:click on:focus on:blur on:mouseenter on:mouseleave on:mousedown on:mouseup {...$$restProps}>
	<slot/>
</button>
```

...then `$$restProps` doesn't contain event handlers, so you don't need to mess around with `handlers` at all. A better conversion would probably be something like this:

```svelte
<script>
	import { createBubbler, handlers } from 'svelte/legacy';

	const bubble = createBubbler();

	let { children, ...props } = $props();
</script>

<!-- @migration task: replace bubbling events with callback props -->
<button onclick={bubble('click')} onfocus={bubble('focus')} onblur={bubble('blur')} onmouseenter={bubble('mouseenter')} onmouseleave={bubble('mouseleave')} onmousedown={bubble('mousedown')} onmouseup={bubble('mouseup')} {...props}>
	{@render children()}
</button>
```

The `@migration task` is there because you can't fix the problem in isolation, you need to update the call sites and the component itself at the same time.


> I think that `<Component on:click />` can be migrated to
>
> ```svelte
> <script>
> 	let { onclick } = $props();
> </script>
> <Component on:click={click} />

That would be breaking, for the same reason — any consumer of that component that had its own `on:click` handler would no longer receive those events (and we can't naively replace the parent `on:click` with `onclick` even if we know that bubbling `on:click` directives will be transformed, because the `click` event could come from an event dispatcher which might not even be defined in `Component` even if we _could_ see it). It should be migrated to use `bubble`, with the same `@migration task` annotation.

Agree with @paoloricciuti that `handlers` should remain in `svelte/legacy`.

Another thing : the `bubble('click')` work fine when props are spreaded after the even, because it can be replaced by the `onclick` used by the caller.

But without spreading, `onclick` will not work as it will not be a known prop.

Exemple :
```svelte
<button on:click><slot/></button>
```
Is migrated into : 
```svelte
<script>
	import { createBubbler } from 'svelte/legacy';
	/** @type {{children?: import('svelte').Snippet}} */
	let { children } = $props();
	const bubble = createBubbler();

</script>

<button onclick={bubble('click')}>{@render children?.()}</button>
```

I agree, I absolutely don't think we should add a compiler option. At most it should be an option passed to `migrate`. 

I think the `let { onclick = bubble('click' } = $props()` solution is clever, but I don't think we should actually do it:

- often, the best conversion would be to use `...props`, rather than an explicit `onclick` prop, in which case this actually creates _more_ manual work
- it means users of the migrated component don't need to care about which form they use. But they should care! We want to incentivize people to update their code. Having multiple ways to do things is something we strive to avoid, because it seeds confusion about which way is 'right'. To that end, marking stuff with a `@migration task` comment feels more honest than outputting loosey-goosey code
Reverting that now...i will implement passive and non passive as action for the moment but we can skip move to a comment if we want

Personally I just find that `bubble()` can be difficult to understand and complicate migrations (automatic or manual), since it should be used differently depending on whether we use `...props` or not.
And the "migrated code" will require another migration in the future, in order to remove the bubble() stuff...


```svelte
<!-- Svelte 4 -->
<button on:click on:focus on:blur on:mouseenter on:mouseleave on:mousedown on:mouseup {...$$restProps}>

<!-- Svelte 5 with bubble() -->
<button onclick={bubble('click')} onfocus={bubble('focus')} onblur={bubble('blur')} onmouseenter={bubble('mouseenter')} onmouseleave={bubble('mouseleave')} onmousedown={bubble('mousedown')} onmouseup={bubble('mouseup')} {...props}>

<!-- Svelte 5 -->
<button {...props}>
```

On the other side, the compile option can be simply ignored in the future, allowing us to have a future-proof code, and it can be used to generate warning/error in case of misuse.

Too bad, but just in case, the code is available here : https://github.com/sveltejs/svelte/compare/main...adiguba:svelte:legacy-events
I don't really know why attribute modifiers were ever removed...

issue_context.title: migrate: Merging event handlers adds an unnecessary parameter
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

When this code is migrated:
```svelte
<button
  on:click={() => console.log('a')}
  on:click={() => console.log('b')}
></button>
```
it turns into this
```svelte
<button
  
  onclick={(event) => {
    console.log('a')
    console.log('b')
  }}
></button>
```

which both contains extra whitespace and an unnecessary `event` argument.

### Reproduction

[REPL](https://svelte-5-preview.vercel.app/#H4sIAAAAAAAAA4WMQQqDMBQFryJvo0Jo90EDPUd1ofFbQmN-MD-FIrl7kXbf5QzDHFidpwR9PxCmjaBxixEK8o4npBd5ISgkzrs9TTdnEQ5DGISDtt7ZZ380bdWbynJI7Oni-dHUU92Wv9H8i0x3_W4NFDZe3OpogZY9UxnLBzjgwLKlAAAA)

### Logs

_No response_

### System Info

```shell
svelte@5.0.0-next.247 in repl
```


### Severity

annoyance
comments: Or a temporary utility function similar to `run`

Yes, been thinking that as well; since there might be quite a bit of logic, maybe something like this:
```svelte
<button
  onclick={handlers(
    () => console.log('a'),
    e => console.log(e.type),
  )}>
```

> I don't think that using an action is a good idea, as this wil introduce a new way to use handlers...

What do you mean a new way? Action always existed and the handler function is not that different. The difference is that with an action you can literally register multiple listener just like svelte 4 while with the function you basically have to reimplement the functionality and the bugs that this could introduce are very subtle.

I was actually thinking of a single action that register multiple but to be fair I actually like the multiple action more 🤣

IMHO the point is that this code shouldn't be the most elegant code ever, is obvious that if you want elegant code you should rewrite it yourself. But it should be the most correct. If I'm migrating my code and it introduce a bug in my code because of some quirk of how browsers implements multiple events that would be much worst than a less beautiful code.

I think that an action with `on()` is required for the passive/nonpassive modifiers.
But for all others case the new onevent syntax is preferable.

> I think that an action with `on()` is required for the passive/nonpassive modifiers. But for all others case the new onevent syntax is preferable.

Again, that's the most beautiful output but not necessarily the most correct code.
